name: wayland

engine.notes: Wayland's own build is Meson/Ninja-based, not CMake and not any of crt-port-build.py's own configure/amalgamation/android_host_tool systems -- same class of 'external build' as libcrtgfx/third_party/skia/recipe.json's own GN/Ninja build, and kept alongside it (outside porting/recipes/, which only the generic configure/amalgamation engine globs) for the same reason. libcrtgfx/CMakeLists.txt reads this file's own source.* fields at configure time via CMake's string(JSON ...) and feeds them to tools/fetch_wayland.py as plain CLI flags, exactly matching the Skia recipe's own wiring. The real Meson option set (scanner/libraries enabled, tests/documentation/dtd_validation disabled, cc/ar wiring) lives in tools/build_wayland.py's own default_meson_options() instead -- build *configuration*, not source pinning, and changes far more often than this recipe's own source.* fields do.

notes: Scope, decided 2026-08-24 (explicit user go-ahead after being shown the real workload for each option): Wayland *core* only for this first pass -- wayland-scanner (needs expat, see porting/recipes/expat.json, added the same day specifically for this) plus libwayland-client/libwayland-server/libwayland-cursor/libwayland-egl (the 'libraries' Meson option; 'egl' here is Wayland's own thin, dependency-free frontend shim, not real EGL headers -- see tools/build_wayland.py's own notes). wayland-protocols (xdg-shell.xml and friends) is deliberately deferred to a later pass: the agreed crtgfx-wayland-smoke design (see below) only needs core wayland.xml, which wayland-scanner already generates client-side bindings for as part of libwayland-client's own build -- no external protocol package required to prove the external-build pipeline works for real.

Deliberately does NOT touch libcrtgfx's existing Linux window backend (libcrtgfx/src/arch/linux/window_wayland.c, a hand-rolled core-protocol-Wayland+xdg-shell client that intentionally does not link libwayland-client -- see docs/libcrtgfx_wayland_plan.md's own 'Linux Host Adapter' section). crtgfx-wayland-smoke (below) is a wholly separate, standalone test executable that links the real libwayland-client this recipe builds -- proving the external-build pipeline produces a working library, independent of whether/when a future session decides to swap the hand-rolled backend for it. That swap, if it ever happens, is out of scope here and was explicitly deferred when this scope was decided.

Pinned, not floating (matching libcrtgfx/third_party/skia/recipe.json's own policy and its own stated reasoning): source.ref/source.expected_commit are the real commit gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland.git's own `1.26.0` tag dereferences to, captured via `git ls-remote https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland.git refs/tags/1.26.0 refs/tags/1.26.0^{}` on 2026-08-24 (the `^{}` form is the annotated tag's own dereferenced commit SHA, not the tag object's own SHA -- `87cc8a8728a923fc57938faa81ba0e74f34ecdc7`, not `5f430e41167dd359b70fb5e9f584ba2dc058e4cc`). 1.26.0 (2026-07-16) was the latest stable release at pin time. Re-pin by re-running the same git ls-remote command and updating both source.ref and source.expected_commit (and this note's own date), never by reverting either to empty/floating.

source.sparse_paths is empty (a full, non-sparse checkout): confirmed for real (2026-08-24) that the whole upstream repo is small (a handful of MB, no vendored third-party content or generated-doc assets the way Skia's own repo has) -- no need for Skia's own cone-mode trimming machinery here. --depth 1 alone (see tools/fetch_wayland.py) already keeps this fetch small.

source.sync_deps is false and stays false: Wayland has no DEPS-style third-party dependency-sync step at all (unlike Skia's git-sync-deps) -- this field only exists so this recipe's own schema shape matches libcrtgfx/third_party/skia/recipe.json's exactly, for whoever reads both side by side.

expat (porting/recipes/expat.json, shared-pass on Linux/Windows as of 2026-08-24) and libffi (porting/recipes/libffi.json, partial on Linux/Windows, configure-pass on macOS -- an existing port, not new) must both already be installed before this recipe's Meson configure step: wayland-scanner's own src/meson.build unconditionally does `dependency('expat')`, and the 'libraries' option needs `dependency('libffi')` (wayland-server's connection.c/event-loop.c and wayland-client both use it). Both recipes already install into the *same* shared port_prefix per preset build directory (crt-port-build.py's own convention -- every porting/recipes/*.json port lands in one out/<preset>/port-tests/install), so tools/build_wayland.py's own single --port-prefix flag (not two separate ones) points Meson's pkg-config resolution at that one shared prefix's lib/pkgconfig, where both expat.pc and libffi.pc already coexist once each port has been built there.

When this recipe is next touched: verify this note's own workload/scope claims still hold before extending it (e.g. adding wayland-protocols later should get its own dated note here, matching this file's own established discipline, not a silent edit to the notes above).
